text: 48-year-old woman. The patient noticed a mass in her left breast 4 weeks ago, which has rapidly increased in size. She denies any recent trauma or infections. No history of similar complaints in the past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any nipple discharge, skin changes like dimpling or redness, or have you noticed any swollen lymph nodes in your armpit? speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Breast Examination: Inspection shows no skin changes, nipple retraction, or discharge. Palpation reveals a 6-cm, nontender, multinodular mass in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast with no palpable axillary or cervical lymphadenopathy. Mammography Findings: Smooth polylobulated mass in the left breast. Biopsy Microscopic Description: Image shows leaf-like structures with stromal cellular overgrowth.

speaker: Doctor
text:
